prompts.text: The JARVIS swarm architecture operates as follows. Each participating model, referred to as a node, receives the same turn input and generates an independent response. The responses are encoded as hyperdimensional vectors using the H D C encoder. The vectors are written to the stigmergy field via the Convex backend. A consensus query then retrieves all vectors from the current turn, computes pairwise cosine similarity, and identifies the cluster centroid. The node whose response vector is closest to the centroid is selected as the primary output. If no node exceeds the similarity threshold of zero point eight five, the turn is flagged for human review. The pheromone field decays at a configurable rate between turns, which prevents stale consensus states from persisting across context windows.
